{{Short description|Complexity class}}In [[computational complexity theory]], '''SC''' (Steve's Class, named after [[Stephen Cook]])<ref>{{ComplexityZoo|SC|S#sc}}</ref> is the [[complexity class]] of problems solvable by a [[deterministic Turing machine]] in polynomial time (class '''[[P_(complexity)|P]]''') and polylogarithmic space (class '''[[PolyL]]''') (that is, [[Big O notation|O]]((log ''n'')<sup>k</sup>) space for some constant ''k''). It may also be called '''DTISP(poly, polylog)''', where '''DTISP''' stands for ''deterministic time and space''. The definition of '''SC''' differs from '''P''' &cap; '''PolyL''', since for the former, it is required that a single algorithm runs in both polynomial time and polylogarithmic space; while for the latter, two separate algorithms will suffice: one that runs in polynomial time, and another that runs in polylogarithmic space. It is unknown whether '''SC''' and '''P''' &cap; '''PolyL''' are equivalent.

'''[[Deterministic context-free language|DCFL]]''', the strict subset of [[context-free language]]s recognized by [[deterministic pushdown automaton|deterministic pushdown automata]], is contained in '''SC''', as shown by Cook in 1979.<ref>S. A. Cook. Deterministic CFL's are accepted simultaneously in polynomial time and log squared space. Proceedings of ACM STOC'79, pp. 338&ndash;345. 1979.</ref> It is open if all context-free languages can be recognized in '''SC''', although they are known be in '''P''' &cap; '''PolyL'''.<ref>[https://cstheory.stackexchange.com/questions/8679/ TCS Stack Exchange: CFG parsing using o(n^2) space]</ref>

It is open whether directed [[st-connectivity]] is in '''SC''', although it is known to be in '''P''' &cap; '''PolyL''': [[depth first search]] solves it in polynomial time and [[Savitch's theorem]] provides a solution on space <math>O(\log^2 n)</math>. This question is equivalent to '''[[NL (complexity)|NL]]''' ⊆ '''SC'''.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Chakraborty | first1 = Diptarka
 | last2 = Tewari | first2 = Raghunath
 | arxiv = 1501.05828
 | doi = 10.1145/3154857
 | issue = 4
 | journal = ACM Transactions on Computation Theory
 | pages = 19:1–19:11
 | title = An <math>O(n^{\varepsilon})</math> space and polynomial time algorithm for reachability in directed layered planar graphs
 | volume = 9
 | year = 2018}}</ref>

'''[[RL (complexity)|RL]]''' and '''[[BPL (complexity)|BPL]]''' are classes of problems acceptable by [[probabilistic Turing machines]] in logarithmic space and polynomial time. [[Noam Nisan]] showed in 1992 the weak [[derandomization]] result that both are contained in '''SC'''.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Nisan | first = Noam | author-link = Noam Nisan
 | contribution = RL ⊆ SC
 | doi = 10.1145/129712.129772
 | location = Victoria, British Columbia, Canada
 | pages = 619–623
 | title = Proceedings of the 24th ACM Symposium on Theory of computing (STOC '92)
 | year = 1992| s2cid = 11651375 | doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> In other words, given ''polylogarithmic'' space, a deterministic machine can simulate ''logarithmic'' space probabilistic algorithms.
